This month, Sabin President of Research & Development Kelly Warfield and CEO Amy Finan traveled to Addis Ababa to meet with officials from the Ethiopia Ministry of Health, Armauer Hansen Research Institute, Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations - CEPI, IQVIA, U.S. CDC, and other partners.  The conversations focused on lessons learned from the 2025 Marburg outbreak response, which included Sabin’s cAd3-Marburg Vaccine in a Phase 2 clinical trial. From supply chains and infrastructure to community engagement, data management and health workforce training, the visit offered valuable insights into what it takes to move quickly, collaboratively, and effectively during an outbreak response.

It is estimated a further 1.5 million lives could be saved annually with better global vaccine coverage. Stop TB Partnership and Sabin Vaccine Institute have entered into a groundbreaking new partnership bringing together TB and Essential Programme on Immunization (EPI) communities within countries to support readiness when the new tuberculosis (#TB) vaccines are introduced.  #Tuberculosis remains the world’s deadliest infectious disease, causing an estimated 1.25 to 1.5 million deaths each year. Infants and children are at particularly high risk, as are people with weakened immune systems. The partnership comes at a crucial time, as countries look ahead to new vaccine candidates that could better protect adolescents and adults, who account for the majority of TB transmission, and offer stronger protection against drug-resistant TB.   Stop TB Partnership and Sabin's Boost Community are uniquely primed to connect the immunization and TB communities, to facilitate the generation of actionable evidence, and to build the relationships and shared knowledge needed for an effective preparation and roll-out by countries. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing health threat worldwide. 🦠  AMR happens when bacteria and viruses encounter antibiotics and become resistant to them, no longer responding to the medicines designed to kill them. Infections become harder to treat, increasing the risk of disease spread, severe illness, and death.  #VaccinesWork to prevent AMR by preventing disease and therefore preventing antibiotic use, lowering the chances for resistant bacteria to develop and spread. Switching from one vaccine to another is just a matter of out with the old, in with the new, right? Not exactly.   As more than 30 co-authors, including Sabin's Kate Hopkins, PhD, MPH, report in "Accelerating Evidence-Informed Vaccine Introductions: Lessons from the Hexavalent Early Adopters Workshop" in the new issue of the journal Vaccines, there are multiple considerations when bringing a new immunization into a country's immunization schedule, including complex system changes requiring coordinated governance, reliable data systems, domestic financing, and multisectoral collaboration.  The paper presents evidence-based insights on making a successful switch from National Immunization Technical Advisory Groups (NITAGs) and Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) programs of 10 African countries, as well as World Health Organization African Region, Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, and consortium partners, who gathered in Senegal last November. It shows the power of Sabin's Regional Peer Learning model/capabilities and helps strengthen policy and operational readiness for countries at different stages of decision-making, planning, and implementation.  See the new article: https://ow.ly/ShmS50Z2nva
